changedBeliefs: `resqlite_json_write_string`'s SWAR escape scan is no longer all-or-nothing. Before exp 235 the SWAR 8-byte fast-skip broke to the byte-by-byte path on the first escapable byte and never returned, so one escape near the start of a long TEXT value forced the entire tail onto the one-byte-at-a-time loop. Exp 235 re-enters the SWAR skip after each dirty chunk, so a sparse escape only downgrades the single 8-byte chunk that contains it.

Sparse-escape TEXT was a real, previously-invisible headroom pocket in selectBytes. The pre-235 harness had `escaped` (dense, ~1/3 escapable) and `lateEscape` (escape at the very end) lanes; neither exercised the resume inefficiency, so the win did not appear until `sparseNewline` (a newline every ~80 bytes, realistic multi-line text) and `sparseEarly` lanes were added. Load-bearing 256B sparse-newline reproduced -23.4% across the order flip; sparse-early lanes reproduced -44%.

The escape-free common path is unchanged. Keeping baseline's tight inner `while (i + 8 <= len)` SWAR loop (one bounds check per clean chunk) means pure-safe long ASCII stays byte-identical and measures as parity; two earlier candidate structures (retry-SWAR-per-safe-byte, and a single outer `while (i < len)` with a doubled bounds check) both regressed the safe/dense-24B guards +7-9% before this structure collapsed them to noise.

The resume fix carries a bounded, pathological-only cost: dense-escape 256B text (~1/3 escapable bytes) is +6.0% from one extra SWAR probe per all-dirty chunk. That distribution is not natural text and is not in the release suite.
nextSignals: `benchmark/experiments/select_bytes_text_string_reserve.dart` now carries `sparseNewline` and `sparseEarly` modes at 256B and 1KiB; these are the durable gate for any future TEXT-escape-scan work. The 256B sparse-newline lane is the load-bearing decision row; dense-escape and pure-safe lanes are guards.

The signals-named SIMD JSON escape scan (exp 229 nextSignal, for the safe-prefix scan *speed*) is still open and is a distinct mechanism from this resume fix. If it is revisited, it must also resume after escapes (the reason exp 230 was rejected at its 256B cutoff was a safe-prefix-only NEON scan that did not restart), and it must clear the same sparse-newline gate, not just the pure-safe lane.
Do not reopen the dense-escape +6% unless a real workload or profile shows dense-escape TEXT (>= ~1/3 escapable bytes) is a hot path; it is a pathological guard, not a target.

General lesson for future scan/vectorise work on any per-element formatter: a fast-scan that abandons itself on the first miss silently penalises sparse-miss inputs across the whole tail. Prefer resuming the fast path after the miss region when the miss is sparse.

claims.text: json_write_string's SWAR escape scan re-enters the 8-byte fast skip after each dirty chunk instead of abandoning it on the first escapable byte, so a sparse escape downgrades only the chunk containing it rather than the whole tail. Realistic multi-line TEXT encodes 23% faster (256B, newline every ~80B) and the one-early-escape extreme 45%; the escape-free path is byte-identical and measures parity. Cost is +6.0% on pathological dense-escape 256B (~1/3 escapable bytes), one extra SWAR probe per all-dirty chunk.
